tools.title: Cancel Render
tools.description: Cancel an in-flight render (stop a runaway/queued job). Needs projectId + renderId (from create_render). No-op if already terminal.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

tools.name: cancel_compose
tools.title: Cancel Compose
tools.description: Cancel an in-flight compose job (stop a runaway/mis-priced ensemble). Needs projectId + composeJobId (from compose). The director cancel is confirmed before the row flips; any linked charge is released. No-op-reject (422) if already terminal.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.title: Cancel Job
tools.description: Cancel a running async job (verify / preview / brand-kit-extract) returned by an enqueue call — abort a mis-priced job instead of waiting out its TTL. For box-backed jobs the warm box is reaped best-effort; cancel never meters. No-op-reject (422) if already terminal.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

tools.name: cancel_export
tools.title: Cancel Export
tools.description: Cancel an in-flight NLE export (fcpxml/premiere). Needs projectId + exportId (from the export enqueue). No-op-reject (422) if already terminal.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

tools.name: retry_render
tools.title: Retry Render
tools.description: Re-render an existing render job's FROZEN composition snapshot — it inherits that job's exact composition/intent/priority and queues a fresh renderJob; it does NOT re-read the project's current composition. So it only helps a TRANSIENT failure (the failed render's `retryable:true` / `category:"transient"` — a flaky pipeline/infra fault): re-attempting the same snapshot may succeed. For a DETERMINISTIC failure (`retryable:false` / `category:"authoring"` — a bad param, an unresolvable media/brand ref), retry_render reproduces the SAME failure: FIX the composition first via apply_composition, then create_render (a retry alone is futile). Check `retryable` on getRender / wait_job to pick the path. Returns the new render; then wait_job(kind="render", id=<new id>).

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

progress.description: Non-terminal render progress; phase is one of the worker's emitted stages.

error.description: Human-readable failure message. Pair with `errorCode` for a stable, machine-readable code an agent runner can branch on.

errorCode.description: Stable, machine-readable error code (e.g. `render_pipeline_unavailable`, `render_route_missing`, `render_pipeline_failed`). Null when status is not `error` or unavailable for an older render.

errorDetails.description: Structured failure context — `{ targetUrl?, upstreamStatus?, upstreamCode?, attemptedAt? }`. Surfaced so agent runners can distinguish operator-config issues from upstream-down vs route-missing without parsing `error`.

category.description: Failure taxonomy when status is `error`; null otherwise. `authoring` = deterministic defect in YOUR composition/request — fix it, retrying is futile; `transient` = temporary pipeline/infra failure — safe to retry_render; `internal` = unexpected server fault — retry once then escalate. Mirrors the render.failed webhook's `category`.

retryable.description: Whether re-attempting the SAME render can succeed (status `error`); null otherwise. true → call retry_render. false → deterministic (category authoring/internal); fix the composition first — retry_render alone reproduces it. Mirrors the render.failed webhook's `retryable`.

updatedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the render's most recent progress update. Compute staleness = now − updatedAt to distinguish a wedged render from a slow one and decide whether to wait, cancel, or retry.

compositionId.description: The composition this render froze at create time (the project's active one, or the compositionId the request named). Null on renders minted before this was recorded.

format.description: The resolved output format the render was encoded at (aspectRatio, fps, resolution): the frozen composition's, after any create-time scale override. Null on legacy rows.

engine.description: The render engine the row was minted for. Null on rows minted before the engine was recorded.

completedAt.description: ISO-8601 instant the render reached its terminal status (complete, error or cancelled); null while it runs. Pair with createdAt for the wall time.

outputDurationSec.description: The output's length in seconds (the composition timeline's, or the preview window's), as billed. Null on legacy rows.

preview.description: The scoped preview window when this is a preview_clip render; null for a full deliverable.

listUsd.description: A2 money stamp: the metered event's LIST price (USD), stamped at the success terminal (exports for deliverable renders, compose_capture for A8 previews). A plan allowance may zero the actual invoice line — this is the list price, never a Stripe charge. Absent while running, on failure, and for x402 orgs (on-chain receipts). Mirrors the get_usage ledger.

warnings.description: Non-fatal advisories surfaced at render-CREATE (omitted when none, and on GET — create-time only).

tools.name: get_account
tools.title: Get Account
tools.description: ORIENT FIRST — show THIS key's account before you spend a metered call: the org it is bound to, the current plan, a per-feature entitlements map, and per-call cost ceilings. READ `balance`, NOT `included`. CueFrame is credit-funded: rendering (entitlements.exports), generation (generate), preview stills (compose_capture), the judge (compose_verify) and the Director (compose) have NO separate per-plan allowance — they all spend one shared wallet, named in `fundedBy` (`credits`; generation is metered in provider-cost units against that wallet). Each `balance` restates that ONE wallet in that feature's own unit at `creditCost` credits per unit, so they are alternative ways to spend the same money, not four budgets. Each entitlement also carries `listUsdPerUnit`: the dollar quote for ONE unit before you call (0 = a plan grant that draws no credits, e.g. resource_import — stock search + import are free; null = not quotable up front). Check the requested cost against the balance. For generation, also check generationLimit: free accounts have a separate provider-cost cap even with a positive wallet. A billing_required error with reason free_generation_cap requires a credit-pack purchase through normal checkout. `included:false` means the plan genuinely lacks the feature. Every new org starts with a free credit grant, so an account with an empty usage history can still render, generate, preview and score. costCeilings.generateMediaUsdPerCall is the generate_media per-call USD cap. No args — identity is resolved from your key (never echoed from input).

generationLimit.description: Separate lifetime generation cap before a credit-pack purchase. Wallet balance is still shared; generation must also fit this remaining provider-cost allowance. null means unknown.

orgId.description: The org this API key is bound to — resolved server-side from the Authorization credential, NEVER from the request body/query.

displayName.description: Org/customer display name from the billing record; null when not set or unknown.

plan.description: The customer's current base plan/tier. null = unknown (billing not configured, or no active plan resolvable yet).

entitlements.description: Per-feature entitlements keyed by featureId. Covers the billing-gated capabilities: `exports` gates create_render AND generate_media output; `compose` gates compose; `brand_kits` gates create_brand_kit; `resource_import` gates import_resource (a boolean grant: `listUsdPerUnit` 0 — stock search and import cost no credits for a keyed caller); plus ai_tokens/storage/compose_verify/compose_capture/etc. Read `listUsdPerUnit` for what one unit costs before you spend it. Most capabilities are CREDIT-FUNDED — `included` is true and the real limit is `balance`, drawn from the shared wallet named in `fundedBy` (`credits` — generation included; a free org is additionally bounded by a generation cap). So read `balance`, not `included`, to decide whether you can afford a call; `included:false` means the plan genuinely lacks the feature. Check BEFORE a metered call to avoid a mid-workflow 402 billing_required (whose error `details.featureId` names the gating feature).

costCeilings.description: Discoverable per-call cost ceilings so an agent can price/right-size a request before a guaranteed 402.

billingConfigured.description: false = billing is not configured in this environment, so plan/entitlement values are best-effort and may be null (unknown), not authoritative.

surfaces.description: The browser URLs that actually exist, so an agent asked to "show me" can hand the user a real link instead of guessing one from an id. A null means the surface is not built, not that it is hidden from this key.

tools.name: list_plans
tools.title: List Plans
tools.description: List the plan catalog (tiers, intervals, product ids, prices) BEFORE a checkout, so create_checkout requests a real {plan, interval} instead of guessing an id. No args — reads the platform catalog.

plans.description: Every purchasable {tier, interval} and its product id.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.title: Get Usage
tools.description: The A2 usage ledger: every metered billing event newest-first with attribution — featureId, amount, the project/job that produced it, and the event's LIST price in USD (a plan allowance may zero it on the invoice). Answer "what did project X cost this period?" with a query instead of summing your own quotes. Filter by projectId, jobId, and/or a [from, to) epoch-ms window. Requires the billing:read scope.

limit.description: Page size (1..100), default 20. Out-of-range or unparseable clamps into the range.

after.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `pagination.nextCursor`. Forward-only.

projectId.description: Only events attributed to this project.

jobId.description: Only events produced by this job — how to answer "did my failed render post a charge?" for one run.

tools.name: create_checkout
tools.title: Create Checkout
tools.description: Top up the CURRENT org's credit wallet. Body { plan: "credit_pack_10"|"credit_pack_30"|"credit_pack_100" } → returns { url }: a hosted Stripe checkout page to open in a browser and confirm payment. There are no subscription tiers — a pack is a one-off top-up, and it is also the only thing that raises the generation (premium_credits) allowance. Always a URL — an existing saved card is NEVER charged silently; the human confirms on Stripe. The org is resolved from your key, never the body. Requires the billing:write scope. Only send a user here when get_account shows the relevant `balance` at or near zero. Discover the packs with list_plans.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

url.description: Hosted Stripe checkout URL to open in a browser to complete payment. Always present on success — an existing saved card is never charged without confirming here.

tools.name: create_brand_kit
tools.title: Create Brand Kit
tools.description: Create or UPSERT a brand kit (re-POSTing the same kitId updates it in place — this is also the brand-kit UPDATE path). Sets fonts/colors/logo. This is brand step 0 of the workflow: author the kit, then bind it to a PROJECT so colors/fonts/motion theme the output AUTOMATICALLY — pass its kitId as brandKitId to create_project, or attach it to an existing project via update_project (PATCH /projects/:id over REST). Without a bound kit, create_render produces UNBRANDED output. Tenant-scoped (no project arg).

audio.description: Call describe_tool_input with tool "create_brand_kit" and field "audio" for the exact JSON Schema.

motifs.description: Call describe_tool_input with tool "create_brand_kit" and field "motifs" for the exact JSON Schema.

body.description: POST /brand-kits body. Org/user are server-resolved; never accepted from the body.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

tools.name: extract_brand_kit
tools.title: Extract Brand Kit
tools.description: Queue brand-token extraction from a website URL — ASYNC: returns a jobId immediately; then wait_job(kind="brand_kit_extract", id=jobId) for the tokens (colors/fonts/title/description, fetched + regex-parsed from the site's HTML/CSS — NOT a screenshot/vision pass). It does NOT persist — review the tokens, then call create_brand_kit to save a kit. A blocked (private/SSRF), non-2xx, non-HTML, or slow (>20s) URL degrades to EMPTY token arrays (a succeeded job) rather than erroring — JS-rendered SPAs typically extract empty; author the kit manually from the compiled CSS in that case.

body.description: POST /brand-kits/extract body — the website URL to extract brand tokens from.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

jobKey.description: Deterministic identity of the work (content hash of every input the result depends on). Re-enqueueing the same key returns the same job while it runs; a failed key revives as a fresh attempt.

status.description: running on a fresh/deduped enqueue; succeeded when an identical request already completed. Cancelled is part of the shared status vocabulary; identical cancelled work revives to running.

tools.name: describe_composition_ops
tools.title: Describe Composition Operations
tools.description: Discover the exact CompositionOp vocabulary accepted by apply_composition. Omit type for a compact list of operation names and descriptions; pass type for only that operation's JSON Schema. Read this before authoring edits or captions.

type.description: Exact CompositionOp type, such as captions.fromComposition. Omit for the operation list.

tools.name: describe_tool_input
tools.title: Describe Tool Input
tools.description: Return the exact JSON Schema for a body field the tool list abbreviates. An abbreviated field names this tool in its description. Pass that tool and field.

tool.description: Tool whose argument the tool list abbreviates, such as validate_composition.

field.description: Body field named in that argument's description, such as tracks.

tools.name: start_template
tools.title: Start from Template
tools.description: Create a new project from a catalog or org template. The server prepares media and verified mattes before the project is ready. Pass the returned jobId to wait_job(kind="template").

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

tools.name: wait_job
tools.title: Wait for Job
tools.description: Wait for a long-running job and return the resolved result — a bounded long-poll. Includes template preparation (kind="template", id=jobId), media import, render, compose, consult, suggestions and preview. If still running, call wait_job again with the same arguments; work continues server-side.

imageIndices.description: Read these 1–4 original zero-based image artifact indices from this completed job, in this order. Does not render again. Same arguments repeat the same selection; omit for the first four.

kind.description: What to wait on, including template preparation (kind="template").

id.description: kind="media": mediaItemId returned by import/generate/finalize/import_resource. kind="render": renderId. kind="compose": composeJobId. kind="consult": consultJobId. kind="suggestions": mediaItemId. Generic kinds use the jobId from the enqueue receipt.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum wait in ms (default 30 min for render/compose, 5 min for suggestions).

tools.name: preview_card
tools.title: Preview Card
tools.description: Render ONE authored card on its own and SEE it, before placing it in a composition. Pass the same `html` (+ optional `tokens`) you would put in a {kind:"card"} clip; you get the still back as an image. Use this while writing a card — it is the fast loop for catching type that overflows the frame, a headline that collides with a logo, or tokens that did not resolve. Sized to the format you name, so what you see is what that aspect ratio will show. To judge MOTION rather than layout, shell the card with a motion preset and use preview_clip.

projectId.description: projectId (path) — the card is rendered inline; nothing is persisted to the project.

html.description: The card markup, exactly as it would appear in a {kind:"card"} clip source.

tokens.description: Token substitutions the html references (e.g. brand colours, fonts). Same shape as the clip source `tokens`.

aspectRatio.description: Frame to size the card into. Default 9:16 — a card that fits 16:9 often overflows vertical.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

prompts.name: add-music-bed
prompts.title: Add a music bed
prompts.description: Retrofits a music bed (and ambience or SFX) onto an existing composition — license-aware search, correct mix hierarchy, ducking under speech, cuts moved onto the beat. Triggers on "add music to this", "this video feels dead", "put a bed under it", "it needs sound", "add background music", "make the cuts hit the beat", "add some sfx", "the audio is just silence".

prompts.name: brand-reel
prompts.title: Brand reel
prompts.description: Produces a 12–20 second 9:16 brand-identity reel — three-beat arc, bespoke cards in the brand's own type and palette, footage graded into the palette. Triggers on "brand video", "identity reel", "make our brand a video", "turn our brand into a reel", "a video that feels like us", "showcase our brand", "anthem video for our launch".

prompts.name: clip-a-talking-head
prompts.title: Clip a talking head
prompts.description: Cuts a podcast, talk, or interview into shorts that open on the strongest sentence, reframe to the active speaker, and carry transcript-timed captions. Triggers on "clip this podcast", "pull the best moments out of this talk", "make shorts from this interview", "cut this down for social", "find the viral moment", "turn this recording into clips", "the good part is buried".

prompts.name: composing-video
prompts.title: Composing video
prompts.description: Use when choosing how to author or assemble a CueFrame video from footage, product actions, typography, diagrams, original motion or mixed media. For a supplied film use cueframe-reference-video; for a narrow existing edit use cueframe-compose-loop. Also use when an agent is asked to make any video with CueFrame: a product launch, announcement, promo, teaser, social clip, reel, short, explainer, animated explainer, concept video, product or dev-tool demo, walkthrough, or founder/talking-head piece. Triggers on "make a video", "launch video", "promo", "teaser", "reel", "short", "explainer", "demo video", "talking-head", or turning long-form footage into clips.

prompts.name: cueframe-brand-demo
prompts.title: CueFrame — Brand demo recipe
prompts.description: Use when turning a local app into a brand-consistent product demo with CueFrame — extract the brand straight from the repo (colors/fonts/logo/motion), capture a Playwright walkthrough of the running app, and author a branded, auto-zoomed demo whose intro/outro/logo/colors/fonts/motion are frozen by CueFrame's engine — e.g. "make an on-brand demo of my app", "record my localhost and produce a branded launch video". This is the end-to-end brand pipeline over the CueFrame curated tools.

prompts.name: cueframe-cli
prompts.title: CueFrame CLI
prompts.description: Use when editing, clipping, or rendering video via the CueFrame CLI — e.g. "make a 9:16 short from this podcast", "pull the best moments out of this MP4", "render a clip", or any task that calls the `cueframe` binary. Also use when comparing CueFrame against direct-ffmpeg approaches.

prompts.name: cueframe-component-authoring
prompts.title: CueFrame graphic authoring
prompts.description: Use when authoring, forking or customizing CueFrame HTML cards, motion-graphics primitives or reusable native components, including a fork of an exact catalog source. Covers cloud MCP, local desktop and CLI project paths using complete versioned source snapshots. For scene-shot devices and cameras use cueframe-scene-shot. Triggers on "customize the parallax look", "make my own animated lower-third", "fork a CueFrame template and edit it", "author a custom graphic and render it". Use before hand-writing a component from scratch: forking a built-in is usually the faster start.

prompts.name: cueframe-compose-loop
prompts.title: CueFrame preview and revision
prompts.description: Use when previewing, reviewing or revising a CueFrame composition, including a scoped correction, reference comparison or final-delivery check. Also use when an agent should drive CueFrame to a high-quality clip itself: author, look at rendered frames, score with the judge, fix the weakest thing and repeat, over the primitives in the `cueframe-cli` skill. Triggers on "turn this source into a polished 9:16 clip" or "compose and self-correct until it scores well".

prompts.name: cueframe-connect
prompts.title: Connect CueFrame
prompts.description: Use when CueFrame is not connected yet, the user asks how to connect or authenticate CueFrame, or another CueFrame skill is about to call a tool and needs the one-time setup path for Claude Code, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed, Antigravity CLI, Copilot CLI, or an x402 wallet.

prompts.name: cueframe-product-video
prompts.title: CueFrame — Product Video recipe
prompts.description: Use when turning a screen recording (with cursor/click events) into a polished, auto-zooming product video or demo reel via CueFrame — e.g. "make a product demo from this Browserbase capture", "auto-zoom this screen recording to where the user clicked", "turn this walkthrough into a social demo". This is a USE-CASE recipe over the CueFrame primitives in the `cueframe-cli` skill.

prompts.name: cueframe-reference-video
prompts.title: CueFrame reference-video reconstruction
prompts.description: Use when recreating a supplied video or matching its motion, camera, typography, transitions, visual identity or audiovisual timing in CueFrame.

prompts.name: cueframe-scene-shot
prompts.title: CueFrame scene shots
prompts.description: Author a CueFrame 3D world-object shot as canonical SceneShotSpecV2 JSON. Use for devices, meshes, owned static models, captured component or video surfaces, world text, materials, bounded shader fields, camera motion, lighting, focus, and product-shot recipes.

prompts.name: cueframe-storyboard
prompts.title: CueFrame Storyboard: brief → flow
prompts.description: Use BEFORE composing when starting a NEW video from scratch and you need to plan its structure — turning a rough ask ("make a launch video", "30s promo", "an explainer for our API") into a concrete beat flow. Owns the intake + storyboard step: interview the user for the brief, resolve the format from the platform, and plan beats from the leading material and requested format. Triggers on "plan a video", "storyboard", "structure this video", "outline the video", "where do I start", or any new-video ask that has no structure yet. Hand off to composing-video for per-beat craft.

prompts.name: every-format-from-one-edit
prompts.title: Every format from one edit
prompts.description: Derives content-aware 9:16, 1:1, and 4:5 siblings from one finished composition — same edit, every platform, no re-editing. Triggers on "make this vertical too", "I need this for TikTok and LinkedIn", "every aspect ratio", "square version of this", "resize for Reels", "one video, all platforms", "port this edit to Shorts".

prompts.name: extracting-brand-kits
prompts.title: Extracting brand kits: reference pixels → a kit the engine honors
prompts.description: Use when the user says "make my video look like THIS" with a reference video, screenshots, or a moodboard — build a CueFrame brand kit FROM that inspiration so every subsequent compose speaks its visual language. Owns the extraction step: sample the reference's graphics-bearing frames, upload them as exemplars, reproduce each recurring motif as an authored graphic verified against the reference, and upsert the kit with the full language payload. Triggers on "match this style", "like this reference", "use this video as inspiration", "extract a brand kit", "moodboard". Hand off to cueframe-storyboard/composing-video once the kit is bound.

prompts.name: launch-video
prompts.title: Launch video
prompts.description: Turns screen recordings and product footage into a 30–90 second 16:9 launch film — payoff-first hook, real product surface punched in, a building bed or narration, one CTA end card. Triggers on "make a launch video", "announcement video for this feature", "turn this screen recording into a demo film", "product video from these captures", "we're shipping Friday and need a video", "feature announcement".

prompts.name: make-a-social-reel
prompts.title: Make a social reel
prompts.description: Turns footage into a finished 9:16 social reel — hook inside 2 seconds, poster-grade type, a decided music bed, one final render. Triggers on "make me a reel from this", "turn this into a short", "cut a clip for TikTok / Reels / Shorts", "make this vertical", "make a social clip from this video", "the opening is boring", "can you make this pop for Instagram".

prompts.name: rebrand-a-video
prompts.title: Rebrand a video
prompts.description: Swaps the brand kit under an existing video and re-renders — tokens, bumpers, logo, captions, and motion re-theme automatically; hardcoded card values get surgical edits. Triggers on "rebrand this video", "swap the brand", "we changed our colors", "new logo, same video", "make this video match the new brand", "re-theme our launch video", "white-label this for a client".

prompts.name: video-craft-standards
prompts.title: Video craft review
prompts.description: Use when judging whether a CueFrame video's idea, visual form, motion, timing and sound meet its brief or reference (social reel, launch film, brand reel, talking-head clip). For tool selection and scoped revision use cueframe-compose-loop. Triggers on "is this good enough", "quality bar", "what should a finished reel have", "review my video", or any request to make a video when no other skill has stated the bar.
